- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Cover fixed-length BF16 GPT training with activation offload fractions 0, 0.5 and 1. The test runs four decoder layers, two microbatches and three SGD steps, compares losses and all gradients against offload-disabled training, and checks that positive fractions perform transfers while fraction zero does not.

After #7575, the original fraction-zero `Chunk mismatch` failure no longer reproduces on `main`. The `finish_all_groups()` workaround has been removed; this PR now adds regression coverage. Q/K normalization follows the upstream offload tests so the positive-fraction controls use supported, unpacked attention inputs.

## Dependencies

Includes #7399 at `6bd691578a7f8b24640056fb6630ca9557be40e5`, with its reload ordering and queue bookkeeping adapted to the upstream resident-group reload slots. Those production changes belong to the prerequisite; no additional production fix is proposed here.

## Validation

At `351575875328cc17ae828f27949f038ad1246c9b`, including `main` at `d00e888f270e2270da872a9679d490f9411e4ece`, 19 selected GPU tests pass on one shared RTX PRO 6000. These cover the native training regression, upstream partial-offload scheduling, delayed normalization commits, warmup fraction accounting, inline reload ordering and checkpoint storage exclusion. There are no skips in the selected cases.

The same native training regression passes at fractions 0, 0.5 and 1 on `main` without this PR's production changes.

[Commands, rank logs, source revisions and checksum audit](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/896d2c4255db2397ed5eaadfd64814ccfef0581e/gdn-conflict-20261103). Upstream GPU CI has not run.

## Issue tracking

Related to #6757.

## Code provenance

No code copied or adapted from external repositories.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests.
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests.
- GPU kernel determinism registration: not applicable; no numerical kernel changes.
- [x] I have kept the change within existing manager interfaces.
- [x] I have documented the validation scope.
- [x] I have run formatting and lint checks on the changed files.

This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.

Pull request vetters can view their responsibilities [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/vetters).

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/contributors).

Thanks for tracing the scheduler and pool lifetimes so carefully. I’ve removed the extra H2D-to-D2H wait and the test that bypassed normal warmup. I’ve also made #7399 a prerequisite and removed my duplicate fallback wait. Reload ordering and queue bookkeeping now come from that PR.

I took another look at the remaining changes and removed the evaluation-first reset handling, the tensor-growth special case, and the new scheduler argument. The evaluation-first test only showed an internal state difference, without demonstrating a later training failure. Tensor growth also goes beyond what this PR needs.

The fix I’ve kept is in finish_all_groups(): empty transfer queues don’t mean that the current microbatch has finished its forward groups. With fraction zero, that shortcut can advance to the next chunk too early and cause Chunk mismatch during backward.

The new regression uses fixed-length training from the start: sequence 128, two microbatches and three SGD steps. The old code fails at fraction zero on both ranks, while fractions 0.5 and 1 pass. The updated code passes all three.

I also reran the dependent GDN tests and complete Qwen TP2+SP+PP2 training on four A6000s. The logs and commands are here, including the old-code failures and exact commits. #7399 still needs to land first.

**[IMPORTANT Correctness rationale] Could you demonstrate why this additional H2D-to-D2H dependency is needed under the actual training scheduler?**

We traced the pool lifetime and the existing stream dependencies. Under the configurations checked so far, we could not establish a reachable overwrite of a CPU buffer whose previous H2D read is still unordered with the new D2H:

- The shared pool is bucketed by `(shape, dtype)` and uses FIFO reuse (`free: append`, `allocate: popleft`). Returning a buffer immediately after enqueueing H2D does not by itself establish that the next forward will reuse that buffer before a consumer has waited for its reload.
- For PP1 combined scheduling, with one pooled offload scope and one fixed-shape tensor per layer, the first training warmup iteration offloads all `L` layers. The next microbatch's first forward scope executes before the previous microbatch's first backward scope, so the pool grows to `L+1` buffers and retains them across reset. In warmup, fallback H2D runs on the compute stream; the subsequent forward and the existing D2H wait on that stream provide the H2D-to-next-D2H ordering even when a just-returned buffer is immediately reused. This is separate from the missing D2H-to-fallback-H2D dependency addressed by #7399.
- Even `L=1` retains two buffers in PP1 combined scheduling. In steady state, after F1 offloads to P0 and B0 prefetches/returns P0 for B1, the free FIFO is `[P1, P0]`. F2 takes P1; B1 waits for P0's reload before F3 takes P0. Thus the consumer wait and the existing D2H wait on compute form a transitive dependency.
- We also traced ordinary PP and VPP schedules, including combined VPP. For example, PP2/rank0/L4 retains eight buffers after warmup. After F0/F1/B0, the free FIFO is `[P7, P2, P1, P0, P6]`, where P6 is the outstanding prefetch for B1. F2 takes the first four buffers, not P6.

For validation, we executed the original pool/manager/handler Python methods with fake tensors and a stream/event dependency model, removing only this added wait in the #8243 diagnostic copy. The checks covered L=2/4/8 with PP=1/2/4, VPP=2/3 where applicable, and a separate L=1 matrix; the checked warmup and steady-state sequences did not report unordered reuse. These are source-driven dependency checks, **not GPU training or CUDA numerical tests**, and assume fixed shapes, one pooled scope/tensor per layer, fraction=1, and no CUDA graphs, recomputation, or MTP. They do not prove safety for all supported configurations.

The new UT exercises a different state: it creates an empty pool, manually sets `is_warmup=False`, enqueues H2D from the only buffer, then immediately submits another offload without the normal backward consumer wait. This valid low-level test demonstrates that the added wait protects that sequence, but does not establish that the training scheduler can reach it.

Could you provide the concrete scheduler/configuration that defeats the existing FIFO/capacity/consumer ordering, ideally with an end-to-end regression test following the normal warmup lifecycle and identifying the reused buffer? Our current conclusion is that the necessity of this extra synchronization remains unproven for the checked training schedules, not that it is universally unnecessary. This distinction matters because the streams are shared across chunks: this wait also orders D2H against unrelated H2D work even when their buffers belong to different buckets.

**[SUGGESTION Integration] Please let #7399 own the fallback reload synchronization and remove this duplicate implementation when integrating the two PRs.**

#7399 already orders fallback H2D after the group's D2H. It also removes the group from `_groups_to_reload` when inline reload takes over, allowing the next bulk prefetch to advance to the preceding group. In this implementation, after inline consumption of G2, the queue still contains G2 and the next bulk reload processes that now-empty group instead of prefetching G1. This bookkeeping issue predates this PR, but #7399 already addresses it alongside the synchronization.

Given the review work already invested in #7399, please rebase on it once it lands (or explicitly make this PR depend on it), remove the overlapping fallback wait, and retain this PR's distinct forward-only warmup, fraction-zero, and forward-chunk progression fixes and their regression tests. The target branch must contain #7399 or an equivalent fallback fix before this PR lands without this wait.

+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="CUDA is required for offload ordering.")
+def test_inline_reload_is_ordered_after_the_groups_offload():
+    """The inline ``tensor_pop`` reload must wait on its group's D2H and then hand the group back
+    from the reload LIFO, so the next prefetch advances to the group backward runs next.
+
+    Two forward-ordered groups are what make the second half visible. Backward reaches ``g2``
+    first and pops it inline; the next ``bulk_reload`` then has to target ``g1``. With a single
+    group nothing ever asks the prefetch to advance, so dropping the LIFO bookkeeping leaves the
+    values correct and the test green while warmup keeps re-targeting drained groups.
+    """
+    off_interface.reset_instance()
+    try:
+        manager = PipelineOffloadManager.get_instance()
+        handler = ChunkOffloadHandler(
+            min_offloaded_tensor_size=0, cpu_tensor_pool=manager.cpu_tensor_pool
+        )
+        name = "core_attn"
+        numel = 4 * 1024 * 1024
+        tensors = [torch.randn(numel, device="cuda") for _ in range(2)]
+
+        # Warm the pinned pool before stalling. First-touch allocation of a staging buffer costs
+        # more wall time than the stall below, so leaving it inside the commit would let both
+        # D2H copies land before the pop and silently disarm the ordering check.
+        warmed = [
+            manager.cpu_tensor_pool.allocate(torch.Size([numel]), dtype=tensors[0].dtype)
+            for _ in range(2)
+        ]
+        for buffer in warmed:
+            manager.cpu_tensor_pool.free(buffer)
+
+        # Stall d2h_stream ahead of both commits, so neither group's D2H has provably run when
+        # the pop below fires.
+        with torch.cuda.stream(handler.d2h_stream):
+            torch.cuda._sleep(1_000_000_000)
+
+        tags = []
+        for tensor in tensors:
+            handler.on_group_start_forward(name)
+            tag = handler.tensor_push(tensor)
+            assert not isinstance(tag, torch.Tensor), "tensor was not managed by the handler"
+            handler.on_group_commit_forward(name, [])
+            tags.append(tag)
+
+        first_group, second_group = handler.offload_groups
+        first_tag, second_tag = tags
+        assert isinstance(first_group._tensors[first_tag], tuple), "group 1 was not offloaded"
+        assert isinstance(second_group._tensors[second_tag], tuple), "group 2 was not offloaded"
+        assert handler._groups_to_reload == [
+            first_group,
+            second_group,
+        ], "both groups should be queued for reload in forward order"
+        assert not second_group._offload_event.query(), "the d2h_stream stall did not take effect"
+
+        # Backward reaches the second group first and finds no prefetch: the inline path.
+        reloaded = handler.tensor_pop(second_tag)
+        torch.cuda.current_stream().synchronize()
+        assert second_group._offload_event.query(), (
+            "the inline reload finished before this group's D2H did: the H2D read the pinned "
+            "buffer before the D2H filled it"
+        )
+        assert torch.equal(reloaded, tensors[1]), "the inline reload returned the wrong values"
+
+        # The inline pop must also release the group, or every later prefetch re-targets a
+        # drained one and the groups still to be backwarded are never reloaded.
+        assert handler._groups_to_reload == [
+            first_group
+        ], "the inline-consumed group was left on the reload LIFO"
+        handler.bulk_reload()
+        assert not isinstance(
+            first_group._tensors[first_tag], tuple
+        ), "the next prefetch did not advance to the group backward runs next"
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()
+        assert torch.equal(
+            handler.tensor_pop(first_tag), tensors[0]
+        ), "the prefetched reload returned the wrong values"
+    finally:
+        torch.cuda.synchronize()

**[IMPORTANT Correctness rationale] Could you demonstrate why this additional H2D-to-D2H dependency is needed under the actual training scheduler?**

We traced the pool lifetime and the existing stream dependencies. Under the configurations checked so far, we could not establish a reachable overwrite of a CPU buffer whose previous H2D read is still unordered with the new D2H:

- The shared pool is bucketed by `(shape, dtype)` and uses FIFO reuse (`free: append`, `allocate: popleft`). Returning a buffer immediately after enqueueing H2D does not by itself establish that the next forward will reuse that buffer before a consumer has waited for its reload.
- For PP1 combined scheduling, with one pooled offload scope and one fixed-shape tensor per layer, the first training warmup iteration offloads all `L` layers. The next microbatch's first forward scope executes before the previous microbatch's first backward scope, so the pool grows to `L+1` buffers and retains them across reset. In warmup, fallback H2D runs on the compute stream; the subsequent forward and the existing D2H wait on that stream provide the H2D-to-next-D2H ordering even when a just-returned buffer is immediately reused. This is separate from the missing D2H-to-fallback-H2D dependency addressed by #7399.
- Even `L=1` retains two buffers in PP1 combined scheduling. In steady state, after F1 offloads to P0 and B0 prefetches/returns P0 for B1, the free FIFO is `[P1, P0]`. F2 takes P1; B1 waits for P0's reload before F3 takes P0. Thus the consumer wait and the existing D2H wait on compute form a transitive dependency.
- We also traced ordinary PP and VPP schedules, including combined VPP. For example, PP2/rank0/L4 retains eight buffers after warmup. After F0/F1/B0, the free FIFO is `[P7, P2, P1, P0, P6]`, where P6 is the outstanding prefetch for B1. F2 takes the first four buffers, not P6.

For validation, we executed the original pool/manager/handler Python methods with fake tensors and a stream/event dependency model, removing only this added wait in the #8243 diagnostic copy. The checks covered L=2/4/8 with PP=1/2/4, VPP=2/3 where applicable, and a separate L=1 matrix; the checked warmup and steady-state sequences did not report unordered reuse. These are source-driven dependency checks, **not GPU training or CUDA numerical tests**, and assume fixed shapes, one pooled scope/tensor per layer, fraction=1, and no CUDA graphs, recomputation, or MTP. They do not prove safety for all supported configurations.

The new UT exercises a different state: it creates an empty pool, manually sets `is_warmup=False`, enqueues H2D from the only buffer, then immediately submits another offload without the normal backward consumer wait. This valid low-level test demonstrates that the added wait protects that sequence, but does not establish that the training scheduler can reach it.

Could you provide the concrete scheduler/configuration that defeats the existing FIFO/capacity/consumer ordering, ideally with an end-to-end regression test following the normal warmup lifecycle and identifying the reused buffer? Our current conclusion is that the necessity of this extra synchronization remains unproven for the checked training schedules, not that it is universally unnecessary. This distinction matters because the streams are shared across chunks: this wait also orders D2H against unrelated H2D work even when their buffers belong to different buckets.

#7399 already orders fallback H2D after the group's D2H.
